He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]] before being selected by the Heat with the 14th overall pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]]. He is a three-time [[NBA All-Star]], a six-time [[NBA All-Defensive Team]] honoree, and he helped the Heat reach the [[NBA Finals]] in [[2020 NBA Finals|2020]] and [[2023 NBA Finals|2023]]. He also won a gold medal with the [[2020 United States men's Olympic basketball team|2020]] and [[2024 United States men's Olympic basketball team|2024 U.S. Olympic team]]s. He has achieved the [[List of NBA single-game scoring leaders|second-highest scoring game by a player]] in NBA history with [[Bam Adebayo's 83-point game|83 points]], achieved in a 150–129 win on March 10, 2026, against the [[Washington Wizards]].{{Cite news |last=II |first=Marcus Thompson |date=2026-03-12 |title=Can't we just appreciate Bam Adebayo's accomplishment for a second before all the critiques? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7109993/2026/03/12/bam-adebayo-83-points-miami-heat-criticism/ |access-date=2026-03-12 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} ==Early life, family and education== Adebayo was born on July 18, 1997, in [[Newark, New Jersey]], to a Nigerian [[Yoruba people|Yoruba]] father, John Adebayo, and an African American mother, Marilyn Blount.{{Cite web |url= https://andscape.com/features/miami-heat-bam-adebayo-is-embracing-his-name-and-his-nigerian-heritage/ |title=Heat's Bam Adebayo is embracing his name and his Nigerian Heritage |last=Spears |first=Marc |date= September 30, 2020 |publisher= | work= [[Andscape]].com |access-date=April 8, 2021}} As a child, he was given the nickname "Bam Bam" by his mother when, while watching ''[[The Flintstones]]'' at age one, he flipped over a coffee table in a manner similar to the show's character [[Bamm-Bamm Rubble]].{{cite web |url=http://usatodayhss.com/2015/five-star-forward-edrice-bam-adebayo-picks-kentuckyn-c-state-bam-adebayo-high-point-christian |title=Five-star forward Edrice 'Bam' Adebayo picks Kentucky |access-date=November 17, 2015 |date=November 17, 2015 |publisher= | work= [[USA Today]] |last=Jordan| first= Jason |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151118142526/http://usatodayhss.com/2015/five-star-forward-edrice-bam-adebayo-picks-kentuckyn-c-state-bam-adebayo-high-point-christian |archive-date=November 18, 2015 |url-status=live}} Adebayo moved with his mother to [[North Carolina]] when he was seven.{{cite web |last1=Spears |first1=Marc J. |title=Heat's Bam Adebayo is embracing his name and his Nigerian heritage |url=https://andscape.com/features/miami-heat-bam-adebayo-is-embracing-his-name-and-his-nigerian-heritage/ |website= Andscape.com |access-date=January 7, 2022 |date=September 30, 2020}} He had little further interaction with his father, who died in 2020 in [[Nigeria]]. Adebayo grew up resenting his last name and Nigerian heritage due to the distance from his father. He started to learn more about his Nigerian background at the age of 16 and has since embraced his heritage. Adebayo attended Northside High School in [[Pinetown, North Carolina]], where, as a junior, he averaged 32.2 points and 21 rebounds a game. During the summer, Adebayo joined his [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) team, Team Loaded North Carolina, alongside fellow five-star 2016 recruit [[Dennis Smith Jr.]] He averaged 15.0 points and 10 rebounds per game on Adidas Uprising Circuit.{{Cite web |url= https://www.zagsblog.com/2015/11/01/bam-adebayo-has-sensational-visit-to-n-c-state/ |title=Bam Adebayo Has 'Sensational' Visit to N.C. State |date=November 1, 2015 |publisher= | work= Zagsblog.com |access-date=September 29, 2020}} Later that summer Adebayo competed at the NBPA Top 100 Camp and was named MVP at the 2015 Under Armour Elite 24 game.{{Cite news |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2015/bam-adebayo-josh-jackson-lead-team-to-victory-at-under-armour-elite-24 |title=Bam Adebayo, Josh Jackson lead team to victory at Under Armour Elite 24 |work= usatodayhss.com| publisher= USA Today |access-date=January 30, 2019 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20190131040617/https://usatodayhss.com/2015/bam-adebayo-josh-jackson-lead-team-to-victory-at-under-armour-elite-24 |archive-date= January 31, 2019 |url-status=live}} After his junior season at Northside, he transferred to [[High Point Christian Academy]] in [[High Point, North Carolina]].{{cite web |url=http://usatodayhss.com/2015/hoops-star-edrice-bam-adebayo-reportedly-to-transfer-to-high-point-christian-for-senior-year |title=Hoops star Edrice 'Bam' Adebayo to transfer to High Point Christian for senior year |access-date= November 17, 2015 |date=August 15, 2015 |work= usatodayhss.com |publisher= USA Today |last=Jordan| first=Jason}} In his season debut, Adebayo scored 22 points and 17 rebounds in an 81–39 win over [[New Garden Friends School]]. On December 29, he posted 26 points and 14 rebounds in a 91–63 victory over [[De'Aaron Fox]] and [[Cypress Lakes High School]].{{Cite web |url= https://www.highschoolot.com/high-point-s-adebayo-gets-edge-in-battle-of-future-uk-teammates/15204200/ |title=High Point's Adebayo gets edge in battle of future UK teammates |date= December 29, 2015 |website= highschoolot.com |publisher=| access-date=December 29, 2015}} As a senior, Adebayo averaged 18.9 [[points per game]], 13.0 [[rebounds per game]], 1.4 blocks per game and 1.5 assists per game, and led the Cougars to a NCISAA state championship appearance.{{Cite news |url=http://www.news-press.com/story/sports/2015/12/21/bam-adebayo-makes-big-impact-high-point/77364334/ |title= Bam Adebayo makes big impact for high point |last=Dorsey |first=David |date= December 22, 2015 |work= news-press.com |access-date=April 6, 2017}} Adebayo was named 2016 [[North Carolina Mr. Basketball]].{{Cite news |url= https://247sports.com/college/kentucky/Bolt/Bam-Adebayo-named-North-Carolina-Mr-Basketball-44714435/ |title=Bam Adebayo named North Carolina Mr. Basketball |work= 247sports.com |access-date=April 6, 2016}}{{dead link|date=April 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} In January 2016, he played in the [[2016 McDonald's All-American Game]] and [[Jordan Brand Classic]].{{Cite news |url=http://www.usatodayhss.com/2016/edrice-adebayos-hard-work-earned-him-his-mcdonalds-all-american-jersey |title=Edrice Adebayo's hard work earned him his McDonald's All American Jersey |last=Jordan |first= Jason |date=February 12, 2016 |work= usatodayhss.com |publisher= USA Today|access-date=April 6, 2017}} Adebayo was rated a five-star recruit and considered one of the best high school prospects of the 2016 class. He was ranked the No. 5 overall recruit and No. 2 power forward in the 2016 high school class.{{Cite news |url= https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/171095/bam-adebayo |title=Bam Adebayo - basketball recruiting |work= ESPN.com |access-date= April 25, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160806133941/http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/171095/bam-adebayo |archive-date=August 6, 2016 |url-status= live}}{{Cite web |url= https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2016/bam-adebayo-436 |title= Bam Adebayo, 2016 Power forward |website= rivals.com |access-date= April 5, 2016 |archive-date= July 11, 2017 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20170711195855/https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2016/bam-adebayo-436 |url-status= dead }} On November 17, 2015, Adebayo committed to the University of Kentucky. |url=https://ukathletics.com/news/2016/12/7/5848d34de4b0bd250a65ee38_131467799823510646.aspx |title=Cats Roll Past Crusaders, 87–67 |date=December 7, 2016 |website=UKathletics.com Victory.{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400910700 |title=Adebayo's double-double lifts No.11 Kentucky over Missouri |date=February 21, 2017 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=February 21, 2017}} As the number one seed entering the [[2017 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]], Kentucky would defeat [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]] in the quarterfinals and beat Alabama in the semifinals. On March 12, 2017, Adebayo grabbed nine rebounds to help the Wildcats defeat [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] 82–65 and win the SEC Championship. On March 17, in the first round of the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], Adebayo had 18 rebounds in a 79–70 victory against [[Northern Kentucky Norse men's basketball|Northern Kentucky]]. In the second round of the NCAA Tournament, Adebayo recorded 10 rebounds to help Kentucky defeat [[Wichita State Shockers men's basketball|Wichita State]]. On March 24, Kentucky defeated [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] in the Sweet Sixteen, Adebayo had 12 rebounds in the game. On March 26, Adebayo scored 13 points and seven rebounds in a 75–73 loss in the Elite Eight against [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]]. After the loss in the Elite Eight, he declared his entry into the [[2017 NBA draft]] on April 5, with him signing an agent 20 days later.{{Cite web |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2705653-bam-adebayo-signs-with-agent-will-officially-leave-kentucky-for-2017-nba-draft |title=Bam Adebayo Signs with Agent, Will Officially Leave Kentucky for Awards announced |website=secsports.com |publisher=[[Southeastern Conference]] |access-date=March 19, 2017}} ==Professional career== ===Miami Heat (2017–present)=== ====2017–2019: Early years==== On |url-status=live}} In his rookie season, Adebayo appeared in 69 games for the Heat and averaged 6.9 points and 5.5 rebounds per game. On November 25, 2018, Adebayo had a career-high 21 rebounds and 16 points in a 125–115 loss against the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web |title=Leonard has 29, Raptors win 5th straight, top Heat 125-115 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401070971 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=January 2, 2023 |date=November 25, 2018}} On December 7, Adebayo recorded 22 points and 10 rebounds in a 115–98 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web |last1=Winderman |first1=Ira |title=Adebayo, Dragic power Heat in Phoenix; Dragic to sit out Saturday |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-heat/fl-sp-miami-heat-phoenix-suns-s20181207-story.html |website=Sun-Sentinel.com |access-date=December 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190410130157/https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-heat/fl-sp-miami-heat-phoenix-suns-s20181207-story.html |archive-date=April 10, 2019 |date=December 7, 2018}} On December 28, he scored 18 points in a 118–94 victory against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{Cite news |title=Justice Winslow, Bam Adebayo lead Miami Heat past Cleveland Cavaliers, 118-94 |url=https://www.wkyc.com/mobile/article/sports/nba/cavaliers/justise-winslow-bam-adebayo-lead-miami-heat-past-cleveland-cavaliers-118-94/95-5b31c1f0-d77a-4a99-8ce8-2f274f998dc1 |work=www.wkyc.com |access-date=December 28, 2018 |date=December 28, 2018}} Adebayo played all 82 games, averaging 8.9 points and 7.3 rebounds per game. ====2019–20: Move to starting lineup, first All-Star selection and run to the Finals==== [[File:Adebayo Hachimura (cropped).jpg|thumb|Adebayo in 2020]] After the Heat traded [[Hassan Whiteside]], Bam took on greater responsibilities in his first season as a starter during the 2019–20 season. On December 10, 2019, Adebayo recorded his first career triple-double with a career-high 30 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists in a 135–121 overtime win against the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web |title=Jimmy Butler, Heat rally in OT after Trae Young says 'it's over |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160996 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=December 11, 2019 |date=December 10, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191211083842/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160996 |archive-date=December 11, 2019 |url-status=live}}{{cite web |last1=Beguiristain |first1=Joe |title=HEAT Dominate OT, Down Hawks In Historic Outing |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/atl-mia-game-recap-191211 |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 11, 2019 |date=December 10, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191211130248/https://www.nba.com/heat/news/atl-mia-game-recap-191211 |archive-date=December 11, 2019 |url-status=live}} On December 14, he had his second career triple-double in a 122–118 overtime win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]], scoring 18 points with 11 rebounds and 10 assists.{{cite web |title=Doncic injures ankle, Mavs rally, fall to Heat 122-118 in OT |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401161026 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=January 10, 2020 |date=December 14, 2019}} On December 16, Adebayo was named Eastern Conference Player of the Week for the games played from December 9 to 15, when he averaged 20.0 points, 11.3 rebounds, 8.7 assists per game.{{cite web |title=Bam Named Eastern Conference Player Of The Week |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/bam-named-player-of-the-week-121619 |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 16, 2019 |date=December 16, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191217001911/https://www.nba.com/heat/news/bam-named-player-of-the-week-121619 |archive-date=December 17, 2019 |url-status=live}} On January 27, he recorded 20 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists in a 113–92 win over the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web |title=Adebayo's triple-double lifts Heat past Magic, 113-92 [[2020 NBA All-Star Game|NBA All-Star Game]].{{cite web |last1=Chiang |first1=Anthony |title=Heat's Adebayo, Butler named NBA All-Stars. Adebayo also part of All-Star Saturday night |url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/nba/miami-heat/article239764368.html |website=Miami Herald |access-date=January 31, 2020 |date=January 30, 2020}} On February 15, he won the [[NBA All-Star Weekend Skills Challenge]] competition.{{cite web |last1=Price |first1=Khobi |title=Double the Heat: Derrick Jones Jr. prevails in Dunk Contest amid controversy; Bam Adebayo wins Skills Challenge |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-heat/fl-sp-miami-heat-all-star-saturday-20200216-k3phglxovrbijfhqavihdphff4-story.html |website=sun-sentinel.com |access-date=17 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200217162646/https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-heat/fl-sp-miami-heat-all-star-saturday-20200216-k3phglxovrbijfhqavihdphff4-story.html |archive-date=17 February 2020 |date=16 February 2020}} Adebayo ended the season averaging 15.9 points, 10.2 rebounds, 5.1 assist, 1.3 blocks, and 1.1 steals. In the NBA Playoffs, Bam helped lead the Heat to their first finals appearance since 2014. He scored a playoff career high 32 points, grabbing 14 rebounds and dishing out 5 assists in the decisive 125–113 victory over the [[Boston Celtics]] in Game 6 of the Eastern Conference Finals. After Adebayo suffered an injury in game 1 of the [[2020 NBA Finals]], the Heat went on to lose to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in 6 games. At the end of the 2019–20 season, Adebayo finished as runner-up in voting for the [[NBA Most Improved Player Award|Most Improved Player Award]].{{cite web |title=Pelicans' Brandon Ingram named 2019-20 Kia Most Improved Player |url=https://www.nba.com/article/2020/08/31/pelicansbrandon-ingram-2020-kia-most-improved-player |website=NBA.com |access-date=September 20, 2020 |date=August 31, 2020}} He was also named to the [[NBA All-Defensive Second Team]] and finished fifth in voting for the [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year Award|Defensive Player of the Year Award]].{{cite web |title=Bam Named |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 19, 2021 |date=February 19, 2021}} Adebayo finished the season averaging 18.7 points, 9.0 rebounds, and a career high 5.4 assists while being named to a second consecutive All-Defensive Second Team and finishing fourth in Defensive Player of the Year Voting.{{Cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/news/rudy-gobert-named-2020-21-kia-defensive-player-of-the-year |title=Rudy Gobert named 2020-21 Kia Defensive Player of the Year |website=NBA.com |date=June 10, 2021}} On December 7, 2021, Adebayo underwent right thumb surgery and was ruled out for at least 4-to-6 weeks.{{Cite web |title=Bam Adebayo undergoes right thumb surgery, out 4-6 weeks |url=https://www.nba.com/news/miami-heat-bam-adebayo-thumb-surgery |access-date=May 10, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} web |title=Adebayo scores 38 points to lead Heat past Wizards |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401438136 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=January 2, 2023 |date=November 25, 2022}} On February 2, 2023, Adebayo was named to his second [[2023 NBA All-Star Game|NBA All-Star Game]].{{cite web |last1=Chiang |first1=Anthony |title=Heat's Bam Adebayo named East All-Star reserve. But Jimmy Butler not selected |url=https://miamiherald.com/sports/nba/miami-heat/article272014807.html |website=Miami Herald |access-date=February 2, 2023 |date=February 2, 2023}} On February 8, Adebayo tied his season high with 38 points on 12-of-16 shooting from the field and 14-of-14 shooting from the free throw line in a 116–111 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web |title=Adebayo scores 38, Heat hold off sliding Pacers 116-111 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468980 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=February 9, 2023 |date=February 8, 2023}} In Game 5 of the Heat's first round playoff series against the top-seeded [[Milwaukee Bucks]], Adebayo recorded his first career playoff triple-double with 20 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists in a 128–126 overtime win, helping the Heat to the second round of the playoffs.{{cite web |title=Heat rally again to win in OT, eliminate top-seeded Bucks |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401541240 |website=ESPN.com |language=en |date=April 27, 2023}} In Game 3 of the [[2023 NBA playoffs|Eastern Conference Semifinals]], Adebayo recorded 17 points and 12 rebounds in a 105–86 win against the [[New York Knicks]]. He also joined [[LeBron James]] and [[Dwyane Wade]] as the only players in Heat history to record at least 20 playoff double-doubles.{{cite web |url=https://clutchpoints.com/bam-adebayo-enters-lebron-james-dwyane-wade-territory-in-game-3-win-vs-knicks |title=Bam Adebayo enters LeBron James, Dwyane Wade territory in Game 3 win vs. Knicks |website=ClutchPoints |last=Silverman |first=Steve |date=May 6, 2023 |access-date=May 6, 2023}} In Game 2 of the [[2023 NBA playoffs|Eastern Conference Finals]], Adebayo posted a near triple-double with 22 points, 17 rebounds and 9 assists in a 111–105 win over the [[Boston Celtics]]. He became the 3rd player in Heat postseason history with 20 points, 15 rebounds and 5 assists in a playoff game, joining LeBron James (4x) and [[Shaquille O'Neal]]. Helping the Miami Heat win 111–108, and tie the series 1–1.{{cite web |title=Jokic gets triple-double, Nuggets roll past Heat 104-93 in Game 1 of NBA Finals |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401544846 |website=ESPN.com |language=en |date=June 1, 2023}} However, the Heat went on to lose the next 3 games of the series to lose the Finals in 5 games.{{cite web |title=5 takeaways: Nuggets drop Heat for 1st NBA championship |url=https://www.nba.com/news/5-takeaways-nuggets-win-title-game-5 |website=NBA.com |language=en |last=Powell |first=Shaun |date=June 13, 2023}} He finished the 2023 NBA Finals leading the Heat in scoring and rebounding with 21.8 points, 12.4 rebounds and 3.2 assists.{{Cite web |title=Bam Adebayo averaged 21.8 points, 12.4 rebounds and 3.2 assists in 5 games in the 2023 NBA Finals. |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask/bam-adebayo-nba-finals-2023-stats |access-date=June 16, 2023 |website=StatMuse |language=en}} ====2023–25: First All-Defensive First Team selection and first round exits==== On November 6, 2023, Adebayo put up a triple-double with 22 points, 19 rebounds, and 10 assists along with two steals and two blocks in a 108–107 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web |title=Adebayo has triple-double, Butler scores 28, Heat hold off LeBron and the Lakers 108-107 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401584778 |website=ESPN.com |language=en |date=November 7, 2023}} On January 15, 2024, Adebayo was named the NBA Eastern Conference Player of the Week for the games played from January 8 to 14, his second career [[NBA Player of the Week]] award. On April 24, 2024, in Game 2 of the [[2024 NBA playoffs#(1) Boston Celtics vs. (8) Miami Heat|first round of the playoffs]] against the [[Boston Celtics]], Adebayo had 21 points and 10 rebounds in a 111–101 win. In Game 4, Adebayo recorded 25 points, 17 rebounds and 5 assists in a 102–88 loss against the Celtics. This was his 31st career playoff double-double, tying [[LeBron James]] for most in Heat history. Miami would go on to lose to Boston in five games despite a playoff career-high 22.6 points per game from Adebayo.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401655102 |title=Derrick White scores 38, Celtics top Heat 102-88 to take a 3-1 East playoff series lead |website=ESPN.com |date=April 29, 2024 |access-date=May 2, 2024}}{{cite web |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask/most-playoff-double-doubles-miami-heat-player |title=Bam Adebayo and LeBron James are tied for the most career double-doubles for the Heat in the playoffs, with 31 double-doubles. |website=StatMuse |date=April 29, 2024 |access-date=May 2, 2024}} On July 6, 2024, Adebayo signed a three-year, $165 million contract extension with the Heat.{{cite web |title=HEAT SIGN ADEBAYO TO CONTRACT EXTENSION |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-adebayo-to-contract-extension |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 7, 2024 |date=July 6, 2024}} On February 1, 2025, Adebayo had 30 points, 12 rebounds, nine assists, two steals, three blocks and hit a 19-foot game-winning buzzer beater against the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{Cite web |date=February 1, 2025 |title=Adebayo hits 19-footer at buzzer to cap 30-point outing in Heat's 105-103 win over Spurs |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401705259 |access-date=February 2, 2025 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press}} On March 3, Adebayo recorded a double-double with 19 points and 15 rebounds in a 106–90 win over the [[Washington Wizards]]. It was his 222nd career double-double, surpassing the previous record set by [[Rony Seikaly]] for the most double-doubles recorded in Heat franchise history.{{cite web |url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/miami-heat/heat-news-bam-adebayo-recounts-special-moment-in-record-breaking-night-vs-wizards |title=Heat's Bam Adebayo recounts 'special moment' in record-breaking night vs. Wizards |website=ClutchPoints |last=Weinberger |first=Zachary |date=March 3, 2025 |access-date=March 4, 2025}} On April 18, Adebayo posted 17 points, 11 rebounds, five assists, two steals and five blocks during a 123–114 overtime win against the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in the play-in.{{cite web |date=April 16, 2025 |title=Herro scores 30 points to lead Heat past Hawks 123-114 in OT in play-in and into NBA playoffs |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401766462 |access-date=April 16, 2025 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} The win allowed the Heat to become the first tenth seed team to clinch a playoff appearance.{{Cite web |last=Reyes |first=Lorenzo |date=2025-04-18 |title=Heat a perfect 10, beat Hawks in OT.
